full_judgment:
2. It is the case of the petitioners that by virtue of registered sale deeds with agreement for reconveyance the petitioners sold some land to the respondent Nos.2-5. It is alleged that when the petitioners offered the money and wanted reconveyance, the respondent Nos. 2-5 refused and as a result the petitioners filed 5(five) redemption cases under the provisions of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act before the Upazila Revenue Officer. The aforesaid cases were rejected by the Upazila Revenue Officer on 22-11-1982. Then the present petitioners preferred 5 (five) Redemption Appeals before the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Bakerganj, who, after hearing the parties and perusing the materials, allowed the appeals by his order dated 20-12-23 vide Annexure 'C' to this writ petition. Then the respondent No.2 Abdus Sattar Shaikh filed Review petitions against the order dated 20-12-1983 and on transfer another Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) came to Pirojpur and allowed the Review Petitions by his orders dated 30.5.1985. Against the orders passed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev), 5(five) Miscellaneous Appeals were filed before the Additional Commissioner, Khulna Division, and after hearing the matters the Additional Commissioner, Khulna Division, allowed the aforesaid Miscellaneous Appeals by his order dated 23-1-88 vide Annexure-E. Thereafter, the respondents No.2-5 preferred appeal before the Land Appeal Board and after hearing the appeals the Land Appeal Board dismissed the appeals of the Respondent Nos.2-5 by its order dated 15-8-1989. 

 3. In the instant writ petition the facts are not disputed. From the impugned order itself it appears that respondent No. 2-5 on the date of registration of the deeds of sale executed five agreements for reconveyance of the lands in favour of the present petitioners. The Land Appeal Board found on Review Applications that since the agreements for reconveyance were not registered under section 95(2) of the State Acquisition & Tenancy Act, the present-petitioners are totally incompetent to file applications for redemption. 

 "95A. Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, any transfer of a holding or of portion or share thereof, either by way of an out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey, where the transfer or receives from the transferee any consideration and the transferee acquires the right to possess, and to enjoy the usufruct of, such holding or portion or share thereof for a specified period in lieu of such consideration shall, notwithstanding anything contained in the document relating to the transfer, be deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage for a period not exceeding seven years and the provisions of section 95 shall apply to such transfer whether made before or after the date of commencement of the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Second Amendment) Order, 1972 (President's Order 88 of 1972)". 

 9. We are not unmindful of section 95A itself as because there is a clause that the provisions of section 95 of the Act shall apply in the case of complete usufructuary mortgage as contemplated under section 95A. One may argue that since section 95A speaks that the provisions of section 95 will apply in such transaction, whether before or after the date of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (Second Amendment) Order President's Order 88 of 1972; the agreement for reconveyance should be registered. But on a close examination of these two sections viz, 95 and 95A of the Act, we find, as we have stated above, that this section 95A of the Act should be considered, as far as practicable, independently and other provisions of section 95 of Act will come into play when it will be required for other ancillary matters. But as regards this agreement of reconveyance with a deed of sale, in our view, will not be required to be registered in view of the fact that in section 95A the two things namely, the deed of sale and an agreement of reconveyance shall be deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage. 

 10. On this point we may get some light from the case of Abdul Kader vs. Abdul Aziz, 47 DLR 67. Though the factual aspects of this reported case are different, yet his Lordship, in fact, in disposing of the Revision Case, has considered the provisions of Section 95A along with section 95(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. His Lordship expressed an opinion that an agreement for reconveyance can be specifically enforced and the provision for registration for such agreement as required under section 95(2) of the Act is not applicable. We also hold that in a case like this, such agreement for reconveyance with a deed of sale as contemplated under section 95A of the Act is not required to be compulsorily registered as required under section 95(2) of the Act and, as such, the finding of the Land Appeal Board cannot be sustained in law.
